details: @swirls/cli ships a postinstall hook (`node scripts/install.js`) that downloads a shell script from swirls[.]ai and pipes it directly into a shell, with no integrity or signature check on the downloaded content. On Linux/macOS it runs `curl -fsSL hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install | bash` via execSync; on Windows it runs `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "irm hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install[.]ps1 | iex"` with the installer's full environment (`{...process.env}`) passed through to the spawned process. The hook executes on any non-CI global install (only skipping when `CI` is set or the install is not global), then copies the binary the remote script dropped at `~/.local/bin/swirls` over the package's `bin/swirls` entry and marks it 0755, so subsequent `swirls` invocations run code that was fetched from a remote host at install time rather than anything shipped in the tarball. `bin/swirls` itself is a placeholder that prints the same `curl -fsSL hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install | bash` command, so any environment where lifecycle scripts were skipped still ends up running the remote installer. IOCs: hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install, hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install[.]ps1.
